question: Can an independent 2026 within-character equipment refresh identify a concrete failure mode in effective-skill context capture that changes prospecting output quality, without assuming yield probabilities?
answer: Yes. On June 27, 2026, Loolie reports a displayed prospecting skill in the 320s despite extensive KP and blue profession gear, then unequipping/re-equipping all three gear pieces and selecting gold-quality ore changed displayed skill to 366 (reported required difficulty 365) and produced gold-quality gems, glass and stone. This is a self-reported before/after observation, not a controlled output histogram or proof of a universal threshold. Independently Draggoth reports gold-quality outputs at maximum prospecting skill and silver-quality outputs when short. June 17 Jacara claims similar gemdust drop rates between full-KP and zero-KP characters but supplies no counts or matched profiles. Record UI-refresh state separately from raw skill/KP/gear, and never promote economic E/P.

proposedModellerGuard: Capture displayed effective skill and recipe difficulty immediately before each cast after selecting the exact reagent; record whether UI has refreshed, gear slot item IDs and equipped stats. If a refresh changes displayed skill and quality rank, stratify rather than pooling. Never infer an output-rank deterministic threshold or economic quantity multiplier from these posts.

controlledValidation.question: Does re-equipping identical profession gear change the displayed prospecting skill and output quality for the same exact ore/rank/recipe at a constant client build?
controlledValidation.protocol: On current Retail record build, exact ore ID/rank, spell 1231127, gear IDs, base skill, all KP nodes, buffs, concentration, recipe difficulty and displayed effective skill before/after unequip/re-equip and recipe selection; capture UI screenshots. Separately collect independent zero-inclusive per-cast outputs, output IDs/ranks, actual completed casts and refunds for matched stable-skill contexts. Do not count failed/aborted casts.

blockers: No raw cast counts, ore/output item IDs or rank-separated output histograms
Re-equip intervention coincided with recipe re-selection; cannot isolate root cause
